newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria criticises U.S. over Virginia execution.
newsitem.headline: Austria criticises U.S. over Virginia execution.

text.p: Austrian State Secretary for Foreign Affairs Benita Ferrero-Waldner on Monday condemned the execution of Joseph O'Dell, the convicted murderer killed by lethal injection last week in the U.S. state of Virginia.
"Despite doubt as to his guilt and the appeal of international authorities like the Pope, O'Dell was executed", said Ferrero-Waldner, number two at Austria's foreign ministry.

O'Dell was executed on Wednesday night after a last-minute appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court failed. Defence lawyers had argued that sperm and semen samples recovered from the victim's body could conclusively prove his innocence.
The Pope had also pleaded for clemency and the case became a rallying point in Italy, where demonstrators gathered outside the U.S. embassy to call for an end to the death penalty.
In a statement, Ferrero-Waldner also pledged to boost Austrian financial support for human rights initiatives in developing countries, saying human rights should not be considered a Western luxury.

Ferrero-Waldner, a member of the conservative People's Party, last trod on U.S. toes in November, when she called Washington's veto of a second term for U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali "an extreme position".
